## 4-Day Upper-Respiratory Self-Care Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

Your symptoms fit a common viral cold or allergy flare, and this plan is aimed at comfort, hydration, and watching for warning signs. Because you have seasonal allergies, post-nasal drip may be contributing to the sore throat and dry cough.

## Non-Emergency Home Care and OTC Options
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

### What to do today
- **Rest and fluids:** water, tea, broth, and warm drinks can soothe throat irritation.
- **Salt-water gargles:** 1/2 teaspoon salt in a cup of warm water, gargle several times daily.
- **Humid air:** use a humidifier or steamy shower to reduce throat dryness.
- **Nasal saline:** spray or rinse can help congestion and post-nasal drip.
- **Honey for cough:** 1–2 teaspoons as needed can calm a dry cough. Do not use for children under 1 year.
- **Sleep support:** elevate your head slightly to reduce drainage at night.

### OTC options to discuss with a pharmacist
- **Pain/fever relief:** acetaminophen or ibuprofen for throat discomfort or body aches.
- **Antihistamine for allergies/post-nasal drip:** cetirizine, loratadine, or fexofenadine may help if allergies are driving symptoms.
- **Nasal steroid spray:** fluticasone or triamcinolone can help congestion from allergies, but they work best with regular daily use.
- **Decongestant:** pseudoephedrine may help congestion if you can take it safely; avoid if you have high blood pressure, certain heart conditions, or are sensitive to stimulants.
- **Topical nasal decongestant:** oxymetazoline can work quickly for short-term relief; do not use more than 3 days in a row.
- **Cough suppressant:** dextromethorphan may help if the dry cough is keeping you from sleeping.
- **Throat lozenges/sprays:** menthol or benzocaine products can reduce throat pain temporarily.

### How to choose based on your symptoms
- **Mostly congestion + allergy history:** saline + antihistamine + nasal steroid is often a good starting combination.
- **Mostly dry cough from throat drip:** saline rinse, honey, and a cough suppressant at night may help.
- **Main issue is sore throat:** acetaminophen/ibuprofen, lozenges, warm fluids, and gargles are usually most useful.

## When to Get Medical Care
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg

Seek medical care sooner if any of these happen:
- **Trouble breathing, wheezing, chest pain, or bluish lips**
- **Severe sore throat with drooling, trouble swallowing, or inability to keep fluids down**
- **Fever that is high, persistent, or returns after improving**
- **Symptoms lasting more than 10 days without improvement**
- **Worsening after initial improvement**
- **Sinus pain with thick nasal discharge lasting more than 10 days**
- **Severe one-sided throat pain, neck swelling, or muffled “hot potato” voice**
- **Dehydration signs:** very dark urine, dizziness, dry mouth, or not urinating much
- **New rash, confusion, or marked weakness**
- **If you test positive for COVID-19 or flu and are at higher risk for complications**

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Check local urgent care] https://www.google.com/maps/search/urgent+care+near+Austin+TX
Action: [Button: Symptom checker] https://www.cdc.gov/respiratory-viruses/

## Sources
- CDC respiratory viruses guidance: https://www.cdc.gov/respiratory-viruses/
- MedlinePlus common cold: https://medlineplus.gov/commoncold.html
- NHS sore throat self-care: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/sore-throat/
